newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA bans, fines former Barings director.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA bans, fines former Barings director.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Futures Authority said on Tuesday its had suspended former Barings Securities director James Bax from its register of directors for 21 months.
In addition, Bax has been reprimanded and required to pay 10,000 stg in costs after he admitted failing to take action to remedy control weaknesses in the Barings Singapore organisation.
The SFA also said that Bax had not acted with sufficient speed to investigate properly Nick Leeson's false accounting entries.
Barings Collapsed in February 1995 under the weight of $1.4 billion of losses on unauthorised derivatives trades in Singapore.
Bax's suspension will run from March 1996, the date when the SFA started proceedings against him.

Some former directors of Barings have been banned for as much as three years but the SFA said it had taken into account, among other matters, that Bax had no product responsibility for the trading activities of Leeson nor any knowledge of futures and options trading.
